<div class="guide-header">
  <span class="guide-badge"><i class="fas fa-key"></i> Identity & Access Management</span>
  <h1>Passkeys & FIDO2: The Enterprise Passwordless Authentication Guide</h1>
  <p style="color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 1.1rem;">WebAuthn registration/authentication flows, attestation
    deep dive, synced vs device-bound passkeys, AiTM bypass defense, and production deployment patterns</p>
  <div style="margin-top: 1rem; color: var(--text-muted);">
    <span><i class="fas fa-book-open"></i> 28 min read</span> <span style="margin: 0 0.5rem;">|</span>
    <span><i class="fas fa-crosshairs"></i> Intermediate to Advanced</span> <span style="margin: 0 0.5rem;">|</span>
    <span><i class="far fa-calendar-alt"></i> February 2026</span>
  </div>
</div>

<img src="/images/guides/passkeys-fido2-passwordless-authentication.png"
  alt="Passkeys FIDO2 Passwordless Authentication Guide" class="featured-image"
  style="width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 12px; margin: 2rem 0; box-shadow: 0 10px 40px rgba(59,130,246,0.2); border: 1px solid var(--border);"

<div class="warning-box" style="margin-bottom: 2rem;">
  <strong><i class="fas fa-balance-scale"></i> Research Ethics & Responsible Disclosure:</strong>
  This document is published for defensive security research and educational purposes. Attack scenarios described
  are based on publicly disclosed research. Organizations are encouraged to use this material to assess and improve
  their authentication security posture.
</div>

<div class="info-box">
  <strong><i class="fas fa-file-alt"></i> Abstract:</strong>
  Passwords are the #1 attack vector in 2026 — responsible for 80%+ of breaches via credential stuffing, phishing,
  and brute force. FIDO2 passkeys eliminate this attack surface entirely through asymmetric cryptography bound to
  device hardware. This guide provides a deep technical walkthrough of the WebAuthn registration and authentication
  protocols, attestation mechanisms, the security tradeoffs between synced and device-bound passkeys, real-world MFA
  bypass attacks (AiTM, push fatigue, SIM swap) and how passkeys defeat them, plus production deployment patterns
  for enterprise environments using Entra ID, Okta, and custom WebAuthn implementations.
</div>

<!-- SECTION 1: THREAT MODEL -->
<h2 id="threat-model">1. Threat Model: Why Passwords Must Die</h2>

<h3>1.1 The Password Attack Surface in 2026</h3>
<p>Password-based authentication is the single largest contributor to security breaches. The numbers are
  unambiguous:</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Attack Vector</th>
      <th>Description</th>
      <th>Passkeys Vulnerable?</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Credential Stuffing</strong></td>
      <td>Automated login attempts using breached username/password pairs</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — no shared secret</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Phishing</strong></td>
      <td>Fake login pages harvesting credentials</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — origin-bound</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>AiTM Proxy</strong></td>
      <td>Real-time proxy (Evilginx) stealing session tokens</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — challenge is origin-specific</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Brute Force</strong></td>
      <td>Systematic password guessing</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — no password to guess</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Password Spraying</strong></td>
      <td>Common passwords against many accounts</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — no password exists</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>SIM Swap (SMS OTP)</strong></td>
      <td>Hijacking phone number for OTP interception</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — no OTP channel</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Push Fatigue</strong></td>
      <td>Spamming MFA push notifications until user accepts</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — no push to spam</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Keylogging</strong></td>
      <td>Recording keystrokes to capture passwords</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — biometric/PIN on secure hardware</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Server Breach</strong></td>
      <td>Stealing password hashes from database</td>
      <td class="severity-critical">❌ Immune — server stores only public keys</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<div class="info-box">
  <strong><i class="fas fa-chart-bar"></i> By The Numbers (2026):</strong>
  <ul style="margin-top: 0.5rem;">
    <li><strong>80%</strong> of data breaches involve stolen/weak credentials (Verizon DBIR 2025)</li>
    <li><strong>$4.88M</strong> average cost of a breach involving stolen credentials (IBM 2025)</li>
    <li><strong>15B+</strong> credentials available on dark web marketplaces</li>
    <li><strong>81%</strong> of organizations planning Zero Trust — passkeys are the first step</li>
    <li><strong>Google, Apple, Microsoft</strong> — all three now support passkeys natively across OS + browser</li>
  </ul>
</div>

<!-- SECTION 2: ARCHITECTURE -->
<h2 id="fido2-architecture">2. FIDO2/WebAuthn Architecture Deep Dive</h2>

<h3>2.1 Protocol Stack</h3>
<p>FIDO2 is not a single protocol — it's a stack of three interlocking specifications:</p>

<div class="architecture-diagram">
  <pre style="color: var(--accent-cyan); margin: 0;">

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ FIDO2 PROTOCOL STACK │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ LAYER 3: WebAuthn API (W3C Standard) │ │ │ │ navigator.credentials.create() / .get() │ │ │ │ Browser ↔ Relying Party (your server) │ │ │ └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ LAYER 2: CTAP2 (Client to Authenticator Protocol) │ │ │ │ Browser/OS ↔ Authenticator (USB/NFC/BLE/Platform) │ │ │ │ Handles: PIN/Biometric verification, key generation │ │ │ └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ LAYER 1: Authenticator Hardware │ │ │ │ TPM 2.0 | Secure Enclave | Security Key (YubiKey) │ │ │ │ Private key NEVER leaves this boundary │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ KEY PRINCIPLE: Asymmetric cryptography │ │ Server stores: Public Key (useless if stolen) │ │ Device stores: Private Key (in hardware, non-exportable) │ │ Authentication: Server sends challenge → Device signs with │ │ private key → Server verifies with public key │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 

<h3>2.2 Key Concepts</h3>
<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Concept</th>
      <th>Description</th>
      <th>Security Implication</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Relying Party (RP)</strong></td>
      <td>Your website/service (identified by RP ID = domain)</td>
      <td>Credentials are bound to RP ID — prevents cross-site use</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Authenticator</strong></td>
      <td>Hardware/software that generates & stores keys</td>
      <td>Platform (built-in) or Roaming (USB/NFC key)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Credential ID</strong></td>
      <td>Unique identifier for a passkey</td>
      <td>Sent to server — maps to stored public key</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>User Verification (UV)</strong></td>
      <td>Biometric/PIN check on the authenticator</td>
      <td>Proves the human, not just device possession</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>User Presence (UP)</strong></td>
      <td>Physical interaction (touch button)</td>
      <td>Prevents remote triggering without human</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>AAGUID</strong></td>
      <td>Authenticator model identifier</td>
      <td>Used with FIDO MDS to verify device trust</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<!-- SECTION 3: REGISTRATION FLOW -->
<h2 id="registration-flow">3. WebAuthn Registration Flow (Ceremony)</h2>

<div class="architecture-diagram">
  <pre style="color: var(--accent-cyan); margin: 0;">

┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ USER │ │ BROWSER │ │ SERVER │ │ │ │ (Client) │ │ (Relying │ │ │ │ │ │ Party) │ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ 1. Click │ │ │ “Register Passkey” │ │ │─────────────────────▶│ 2. POST /register │ │ │─────────────────────▶│ │ │ │ 3. Generate: │ │ │ - challenge (random 32B) │ │ │ - rp: {id, name} │ │ │ - user: {id, name} │ │ 4. PublicKeyOptions │ - pubKeyCredParams │ │◀─────────────────────│ - attestation pref │ │ │ │ 5. Browser calls │ │ │ navigator.credentials.create(options) │ │ │ │ │ 6. Authenticator │ │ │ prompts biometric │ │ │◀─────────────────────│ │ │ │ │ │ 7. User touches │ │ │ fingerprint/face │ │ │─────────────────────▶│ │ │ │ │ │ 8. Authenticator: │ │ - Generates key pair (P-256 or Ed25519) │ │ - Stores private key in Secure Enclave │ │ - Creates attestation object │ │ │ │ │ │ 9. Send to server: │ │ │ - credentialId │ │ │ - publicKey │ │ │ - attestationObject │ │ │ - clientDataJSON │ │ │─────────────────────▶│ │ │ │ 10. Server verifies: │ │ │ - challenge matches │ │ │ - origin matches RP ID │ │ │ - attestation valid │ │ │ - stores publicKey + credId │ │ 11. 201 Created │ │ │◀─────────────────────│ │ │ │ 

<div class="technical-box">
  <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Server-Side Registration (Node.js + @simplewebauthn/server)</h3>
  <pre><code class="language-javascript">import {

generateRegistrationOptions, verifyRegistrationResponse } from ‘@simplewebauthn/server’;

// Step 1: Generate registration options const options = await generateRegistrationOptions({ rpName: ‘MyApp’, rpID: ‘myapp.com’, userID: user.id, // Opaque user handle (NOT email) userName: user.email, attestationType: ‘direct’, // Request attestation for enterprise authenticatorSelection: { residentKey: ‘required’, // Discoverable credential (passkey) userVerification: ‘required’, // Require biometric/PIN authenticatorAttachment: ‘platform’, // Or ‘cross-platform’ for keys }, supportedAlgorithmIDs: [-7, -257], // ES256 (P-256), RS256 });

// Store challenge in session for verification session.currentChallenge = options.challenge;

// Step 2: Verify the registration response from client const verification = await verifyRegistrationResponse({ response: clientResponse, // From navigator.credentials.create() expectedChallenge: session.currentChallenge, expectedOrigin: ‘https://myapp.com’, expectedRPID: ‘myapp.com’, requireUserVerification: true, });

if (verification.verified) { // Store credential in database await db.credentials.create({ credentialID: verification.registrationInfo.credentialID, publicKey: verification.registrationInfo.credentialPublicKey, counter: verification.registrationInfo.counter, transports: clientResponse.response.getTransports(), userID: user.id, // AAGUID for authenticator identification aaguid: verification.registrationInfo.aaguid, }); } 

<!-- SECTION 4: AUTHENTICATION -->
<h2 id="authentication-flow">4. WebAuthn Authentication Flow</h2>

<div class="architecture-diagram">
  <pre style="color: var(--accent-cyan); margin: 0;">

┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ USER │ │ BROWSER │ │ SERVER │ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ 1. Click “Login” │ │ │─────────────────────▶│ 2. POST /auth/begin │ │ │─────────────────────▶│ │ │ │ 3. Generate challenge │ │ 4. PublicKeyOptions │ + allowCredentials │ │◀─────────────────────│ (list of credentialIDs) │ │ │ │ 5. navigator.credentials.get(options) │ │ │ │ │ 6. Authenticator │ │ │ checks RP ID match │ │ │ (PHISHING DEFENSE) │ │ │ │ │ │ 7. Biometric prompt│ │ │◀─────────────────────│ │ │ 8. User verifies │ │ │─────────────────────▶│ │ │ │ │ │ 9. Authenticator signs challenge │ │ with PRIVATE KEY │ │ (key never leaves hardware) │ │ │ │ │ │ 10. Assertion: │ │ │ - credentialId │ │ │ - authenticatorData │ │ │ - signature │ │ │ - clientDataJSON │ │ │─────────────────────▶│ │ │ │ 11. Server: │ │ │ - Lookup public key │ │ │ - Verify signature │ │ │ - Check counter (clone) │ │ │ - Verify origin/RP ID │ │ 12. Auth Success │ - Issue session token │ │◀─────────────────────│ │ │ │

KEY SECURITY PROPERTIES: → Challenge is UNIQUE per attempt (prevents replay) → RP ID is checked by authenticator (prevents phishing) → Private key NEVER transmitted (prevents interception) → Counter increments (detects cloned authenticators) 

<!-- SECTION 5: ATTESTATION -->
<h2 id="attestation">5. Attestation: Verifying Authenticator Trust</h2>

<p>Attestation answers a critical enterprise question: <strong>"Can I trust the device that generated this
    passkey?"</strong></p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Attestation Type</th>
      <th>What Server Receives</th>
      <th>Use Case</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>None</strong></td>
      <td>No attestation data</td>
      <td>Consumer apps — maximum privacy, minimum trust</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Indirect</strong></td>
      <td>Anonymized attestation via privacy CA</td>
      <td>Balance between privacy and device verification</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Direct</strong></td>
      <td>Full attestation certificate chain + AAGUID</td>
      <td>Enterprise — verify exact authenticator make/model</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Enterprise</strong></td>
      <td>Device-specific serial number + certs</td>
      <td>High-assurance: government, military, finance</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<div class="technical-box">
  <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Verifying Attestation Against FIDO Metadata Service (MDS)</h3>
  <pre><code class="language-javascript">// Enterprise: Verify the authenticator is on your approved list

import { MetadataService } from ‘@simplewebauthn/server’;

// Initialize with FIDO Alliance Metadata Service await MetadataService.initialize({ mdsServers: [{ url: ‘https://mds3.fidoalliance.org/’ }], });

// After registration, check the AAGUID const aaguid = verification.registrationInfo.aaguid; const metadata = await MetadataService.getStatement(aaguid);

if (!metadata) { throw new Error(‘Unknown authenticator — not in FIDO MDS’); }

// Enforce enterprise policy: only allow FIPS 140-2 certified keys const certifications = metadata.authenticatorGetInfo?.certifications; if (!certifications?.FIPS_140_2) { throw new Error(‘Authenticator not FIPS 140-2 certified — rejected’); }

// Log the authenticator model for inventory console.log(Registered: ${metadata.description}); // → “Registered: YubiKey 5 Series (FIPS)” 

<!-- SECTION 6: SYNCED VS DEVICE-BOUND -->
<h2 id="synced-vs-bound">6. Synced vs Device-Bound Passkeys</h2>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Property</th>
      <th>Synced Passkeys</th>
      <th>Device-Bound Passkeys</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Storage</strong></td>
      <td>iCloud Keychain, Google PM, 1Password</td>
      <td>YubiKey, Titan Key, TPM only</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Cross-Device</strong></td>
      <td>✅ Available on all synced devices</td>
      <td>❌ Only on the hardware key</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Backup/Recovery</strong></td>
      <td>✅ Cloud backup (encrypted)</td>
      <td>❌ Lost key = register new one</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Exportable</strong></td>
      <td>Within ecosystem only</td>
      <td>❌ Non-exportable by design</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Cloud Dependency</strong></td>
      <td>Requires cloud account security</td>
      <td>None — fully offline capable</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Phishing Resistant</strong></td>
      <td>✅ Yes — origin bound</td>
      <td>✅ Yes — origin bound</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Enterprise Attestation</strong></td>
      <td>❌ Limited</td>
      <td>✅ Full (AAGUID, certs, FIPS)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Best For</strong></td>
      <td>Consumer apps, low-medium risk enterprise</td>
      <td>Finance, healthcare, government, privileged access</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<div class="warning-box">
  <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> Security Consideration — Synced Passkey Risks:</strong>
  <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem;">Synced passkeys are only as secure as the cloud account protecting them. If an
    attacker compromises an Apple ID or Google account (via social engineering, SIM swap, or account recovery
    abuse), they gain access to ALL synced passkeys. For privileged accounts (admin, root, financial), mandate
    <strong>device-bound passkeys on FIPS hardware</strong>.</p>
</div>

<!-- SECTION 7: MFA BYPASS ATTACKS -->
<h2 id="mfa-bypass">7. MFA Bypass Attacks & How Passkeys Defeat Them</h2>

<h3>7.1 Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) — Evilginx</h3>
<div class="attack-scenario">
  <p><strong>How It Works:</strong> Attacker deploys a reverse proxy (Evilginx, Modlishka) that sits between the
    victim and the real login page. The victim sees what looks like the real site. They enter their password and MFA
    code. The proxy captures both and replays them to the real server, stealing the session cookie.</p>
  <p><strong>Why Passwords + TOTP Fail:</strong> Both the password AND the TOTP code are transmitted through the
    proxy to the real server. The attacker captures the resulting session token.</p>
  <p style="color: var(--accent-green);"><strong>Why Passkeys Win:</strong> The authenticator checks the RP ID
    (domain) before signing. The proxy domain (<code>login-microsoft.evil[.]com</code>) doesn't match the RP ID
    (<code>login.microsoft.com</code>), so the authenticator <strong>refuses to sign the challenge</strong>. Attack
    fails silently.</p>
</div>

<h3>7.2 Push Fatigue (MFA Bombing)</h3>
<div class="attack-scenario">
  <p><strong>How It Works:</strong> Attacker has stolen credentials. They trigger MFA push notifications repeatedly
    (often at 2-3 AM) until the exhausted user approves one.</p>
  <p><strong>Victims:</strong> Uber (Lapsus$, 2022), Cisco (Yanluowang, 2022), Microsoft (Midnight Blizzard, 2024)
  </p>
  <p style="color: var(--accent-green);"><strong>Why Passkeys Win:</strong> There is no push notification to spam.
    Authentication requires <strong>biometric verification on an origin-bound credential</strong>. The attacker
    can't even initiate the ceremony without physical access to the authenticator.</p>
</div>

<h3>7.3 SIM Swap + SMS OTP Interception</h3>
<div class="attack-scenario">
  <p><strong>How It Works:</strong> Attacker social-engineers the mobile carrier to port the victim's phone number
    to a SIM they control. All SMS-based OTPs now go to the attacker.</p>
  <p style="color: var(--accent-green);"><strong>Why Passkeys Win:</strong> No SMS channel involved. Authentication
    is purely cryptographic — the private key lives in the device's TPM/Secure Enclave, not on a SIM card.</p>
</div>

<div class="technical-box">
  <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Entra ID — Enforce FIDO2 Passkeys via Conditional Access</h3>

{ “displayName”: “Require FIDO2 for Privileged Users”, “state”: “enabled”, “conditions”: { “users”: { “includeGroups”: [“Global-Admins”, “Security-Admins”] }, “applications”: { “includeApplications”: [“All”] } }, “grantControls”: { “operator”: “AND”, “builtInControls”: [“mfa”], “authenticationStrength”: { “id”: “00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000004”, // ↑ “Phishing-resistant MFA” built-in strength // Accepts: FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello, // Certificate-based auth // REJECTS: SMS, voice call, push notification, TOTP } } } 

<h3>8.2 Okta — FIDO2 WebAuthn Policy</h3>
<div class="technical-box">
  <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Okta Authentication Policy — Passkey Enforcement</h3>
  <pre><code class="language-yaml"># Okta Authentication Policy (via Terraform)

resource “okta_policy_rule_mfa” “passkey_required” { policy_id = okta_policy_mfa.security_policy.id name = “Require Passkey for High-Risk Apps” status = “ACTIVE” priority = 1

app_include { type = “APP_TYPE” name = “SAML_2_0” # All SAML apps }

actions { okta_verify { access = “DENIED” # Block Okta Verify push } fido_webauthn { access = “REQUIRED” # Require FIDO2 passkey } sms { access = “DENIED” # Block SMS OTP } voice_call { access = “DENIED” # Block voice OTP } } } 

<!-- SECTION 9: WEBAUTHN CODE -->
<h2 id="webauthn-code">9. WebAuthn Client-Side Implementation</h2>

<div class="technical-box">
  <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Complete Client-Side WebAuthn (Browser JavaScript)</h3>
  <pre><code class="language-javascript">// ===== REGISTRATION =====

async function registerPasskey() { // 1. Get options from your server const optionsRes = await fetch(‘/api/webauthn/register/begin’, { method: ‘POST’, credentials: ‘same-origin’, }); const options = await optionsRes.json();

// 2. Decode base64url fields options.challenge = base64urlToBuffer(options.challenge); options.user.id = base64urlToBuffer(options.user.id);

// 3. Create credential — triggers biometric prompt const credential = await navigator.credentials.create({ publicKey: options });

// 4. Send attestation to server for verification const result = await fetch(‘/api/webauthn/register/finish’, { method: ‘POST’, headers: { ‘Content-Type’: ‘application/json’ }, body: JSON.stringify({ id: credential.id, rawId: bufferToBase64url(credential.rawId), type: credential.type, response: { attestationObject: bufferToBase64url( credential.response.attestationObject ), clientDataJSON: bufferToBase64url( credential.response.clientDataJSON ), }, }), }); return result.json(); }

// ===== AUTHENTICATION ===== async function loginWithPasskey() { // 1. Get authentication options const optionsRes = await fetch(‘/api/webauthn/auth/begin’, { method: ‘POST’, credentials: ‘same-origin’, }); const options = await optionsRes.json(); options.challenge = base64urlToBuffer(options.challenge);

// 2. Get assertion — triggers biometric prompt const assertion = await navigator.credentials.get({ publicKey: options });

// 3. Send signed assertion to server const result = await fetch(‘/api/webauthn/auth/finish’, { method: ‘POST’, headers: { ‘Content-Type’: ‘application/json’ }, body: JSON.stringify({ id: assertion.id, rawId: bufferToBase64url(assertion.rawId), type: assertion.type, response: { authenticatorData: bufferToBase64url( assertion.response.authenticatorData ), clientDataJSON: bufferToBase64url( assertion.response.clientDataJSON ), signature: bufferToBase64url( assertion.response.signature ), userHandle: bufferToBase64url( assertion.response.userHandle ), }, }), }); return result.json(); } 

<!-- SECTION 10: DETECTION -->
<h2 id="detection">10. Detection Engineering & Audit</h2>

<h3>10.1 Sigma Rule — Detect Passkey Anomalies</h3>
<div class="technical-box">
  <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Sigma Rule: Suspicious Passkey Registration</h3>
  <pre><code class="language-yaml">title: Suspicious FIDO2 Passkey Registration Activity

id: f3d2a1b0-passkey-audit-2026 status: experimental description: | Detects anomalous passkey registration patterns that may indicate account takeover via passkey enrollment abuse. author: TheHGTech Security Research date: 2026/02/18 logsource: product: azure service: signinlogs detection: selection_registration: properties.authentication.authenticationMethod: - ‘FIDO2 security key’ - ‘Passkey (FIDO2)’ properties.status.errorCode: 0 properties.authentication.authenticationStepType: ‘primaryAuthentication’ filter_known_locations: properties.location.countryOrRegion: - ‘IN’ # Your expected countries - ‘US’ filter_known_devices: properties.deviceDetail.isManaged: true condition: selection_registration and not (filter_known_locations or filter_known_devices) falsepositives: - Employee registering passkey while traveling - New device enrollment level: high 

<h3>10.2 Audit Checklist</h3>
<div class="success-box">
  <strong><i class="fas fa-clipboard-check"></i> Passkey Deployment Audit Script:</strong>
  <pre><code class="language-bash">#!/bin/bash

passkey-audit.sh — Verify FIDO2 deployment hardening

echo “=== FIDO2/Passkey Deployment Audit ===”

1. Check WebAuthn RP ID configuration

echo “[CHECK] RP ID matches production domain…” RPID=$(grep -r “rpID” /app/config/ 2>/dev/null | head -1) echo “ RP ID: $RPID“

2. Verify user verification is REQUIRED (not ‘preferred’)

echo “[CHECK] User verification enforcement…” UV=$(grep -r “userVerification” /app/config/ 2>/dev/null) if echo “$UV” | grep -q “required”; then echo “ ✅ UV = required“ else echo “ ❌ WARNING: UV not set to ‘required’ — biometric bypass possible“ fi

3. Check attestation mode

echo “[CHECK] Attestation type…” ATT=$(grep -r “attestationType|attestation” /app/config/ 2>/dev/null) echo “ $ATT“

4. Verify HTTPS enforcement

echo “[CHECK] Origin uses HTTPS…” ORIGIN=$(grep -r “expectedOrigin” /app/config/ 2>/dev/null) if echo “$ORIGIN” | grep -q “https://”; then echo “ ✅ HTTPS enforced“ else echo “ ❌ CRITICAL: HTTP origin detected — WebAuthn requires HTTPS“ fi

5. Check supported algorithms

echo “[CHECK] Algorithm support…” ALGOS=$(grep -r “supportedAlgorithmIDs|pubKeyCredParams” /app/config/ 2>/dev/null) echo “ $ALGOS“ echo “” echo “=== Audit Complete ===”
